key_points: Growth is solid but not accelerating: AI capex and loose financial conditions (NFCI -0.54) support activity, while June payrolls rose only 57k and the latest GDPNow reading available (1.7%) is modest.
Consumer sentiment is depressed at 49.5 but rebounding. Low claims (208k) argue against an imminent slowdown, which supports equities and keeps HY spreads tight.
With 2y and 10y yields near 1-year highs, steady-not-hot growth gives limited fuel for further front-end repricing, leaving a slight downside tilt to yields and mild steepening.
The VIX jumped and oil spiked about 15% on the week. Absent a growth shock, both tend to mean-revert, so the near-term lean is toward lower VIX and lower oil.
Dollar, gold and breakevens are mostly neutral from a growth lens.
June CPI fell about 0.4% m/m on the energy drop after the Hormuz agreement. Headline YoY is ~3.5%, but core PCE is still ~0.3% m/m and 3.4% YoY, so underlying inflation is sticky.
WTI jumped 15% in the past week to $83, which threatens the headline disinflation narrative. The 10-year breakeven did not react and sits at the 11th percentile, so the skew is mildly upward.

The Fed has dropped its easing bias, and many participants see a higher rate as appropriate by year-end. The 2-year at the 97th percentile already prices this hawkish lean, which limits further upside in front-end yields absent a core upside surprise.
Sticky core inflation versus falling headline keeps term premium and long yields supported relative to the front end. Slight steepening bias in 2s10s.
Rising real yields and fading inflation-hedge demand keep gold under pressure despite deeply oversold levels.

Wage growth of 3.4% is consistent with disinflation and is not a second-round source. This argues against an inflation scare, so equities keep a mild positive drift and the VIX should mean-revert lower after its recent spike.
Labor market is stable-to-firm: unemployment fell to 4.2% in June, initial claims at 208k are near cycle lows and below year-ago 228k; no sign of loosening.
June payrolls only +57k is soft on its face, but with low labor-force growth FOMC sees job gains keeping pace with the workforce; wage growth (AHE 3.4%) not inflationary.

A firm labor market removes the employment-side case for cuts and leaves the Fed focused on elevated inflation, with some members open to hikes; mild upside bias to front-end and 10y yields, though much is already priced at 1y highs.
Upcoming August payrolls report within the 1m window is the key labor catalyst; low claims argue against a downside surprise.
Solid employment supports consumer spending and earnings: modestly bullish equities, tight HY spreads stay contained, VIX spike after a 1w selloff likely to fade.
Hawkish-leaning real rate backdrop from steady labor is mildly negative for gold and supportive of the dollar; little direct labor signal for oil or breakevens.
Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75% with easing bias removed and a few participants open to hikes; the July 29 meeting is very likely a hold with hawkish tone already priced.

2y at 4.18% sits ~55bp above the funds midpoint, implying hikes are priced. With June CPI falling on energy and labor stable but not hot, the Fed is unlikely to validate hikes before September, giving a mild downside edge to front-end yields.
Front-end-led rally would steepen 2s10s from a 7th-percentile level; term premium concerns cited by the Desk keep 10y stickier than 2y.
Dollar supported by rate differentials but ECB/BoE also hiking, so roughly neutral; slight fade at 3m if US pricing eases.
Equities and credit backed by AI earnings and easy financial conditions (NFCI -0.54); a non-hiking Fed is supportive, while VIX spiked last week and tends to mean-revert.
Gold crushed by higher real rates to a 1-year low; stabilization is likely if hike pricing stops rising. Breakevens anchored near 2.2%, so there is no strong directional edge.

Desk flagged shift in Treasury ownership from price-insensitive official holders to price-sensitive private investors, supporting a structurally higher term premium and a mild upward bias in 10y yields.
Late-July/early-August quarterly refunding falls inside the 1m window; coupon supply and any term-premium repricing should weigh on the long end more than the front end.

Reserve management bill purchases are absorbing bill supply and keeping front-end funding soft, anchoring 2y yields; 2y already at 97th percentile of 1y range with pricing for hikes, limiting further upside.
2s10s near the bottom of its 1y range (7th percentile); fiscal supply and term-premium pressure favor bear/bull steepening over the 1-3m horizon.
Fiscal-supply lens offers little edge for the dollar, oil, breakevens and credit; equities keep mild positive drift despite higher term premium; VIX just jumped ~3.7 pts and tends to mean revert.
Liquidity is ample: Fed balance sheet growing via reserve-management bill purchases, repo traded below IORB in May, ON RRP take-up modest; NFCI at -0.54 signals loose conditions.
Loose financial conditions favor equities and a fading of the latest VIX spike (+3.7 pts in a week) back toward the high teens/mid teens.
HY spreads at the 14th percentile of their 1y range leave little room to tighten; private credit redemptions and BDC outflows are a slow-burn risk, so a mild upward bias over 1-3 months.
Front-end yields near 1y highs with a hawkish-leaning Fed already priced; abundant reserves and bill scarcity cap upside, giving a mild down bias for 2y and modest steepening.
Dollar is firm on rate differentials but is already in the upper part of its range; no strong liquidity-driven edge.
Oil's +15% weekly jump looks stretched against a liquidity backdrop that is not tightening; gold is near 1y lows with high real yields, so roughly neutral.
VIX jumped 3.7 points in a week to 18.8 while S&P fell only 1.6%. VIX futures shorts are moderate (61st percentile), so mean reversion of the spike favors lower VIX and a modest equity rebound.
ES net short is at the 95th percentile, i.e., the least short in a year. Equity positioning is not washed out, but the long-run drift and dip-buying still favor upside.
Dollar index longs are at the 95th percentile, a crowded trade, which gives a slight downside tilt to the broad dollar.
2-year note shorts are being covered (99th percentile, +103k on the week) with 2s10s at the 7th percentile. Short-end yields are near one-year highs, so a mild bias to lower 2y and a steeper curve.
HY spreads at 2.73 (14th percentile) look complacent. With volatility picking up, risks skew toward gradual widening over 1-3 months.
WTI spec length is light (18th percentile) after a 15% weekly spike. This could cut either way, and a spike-reversal risk gives a slight downside tilt.

Gold sits at a one-year low (1st percentile) with only mid-range spec length. That makes it oversold, but there is no positioning catalyst, so the view is roughly neutral with a slight rebound tilt at 3m.
Dollar's 3m gain (+2.1%) was driven by widening US-AFE short-rate gaps; ECB already hiking and BoE hikes still priced, so further differential widening looks harder from here.
Speculative DX longs at 95th percentile of 52 weeks: crowded dollar positioning tilts risk modestly toward USD giveback, though the oil shock supports USD terms of trade.

Foreign central banks prioritizing second-round inflation risks keep global yields firm, while shift in Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private holders supports term premium; 2y at 97th percentile looks more exposed to mean reversion than 10y, mild steepening bias.
WTI +15% in a week on renewed Middle East risk; energy-importing Europe/Asia growth hit, but spikes tend to partially retrace; CL spec length low limits squeeze fuel.
Gold at 1y low after -17% in 3m with a strong dollar and higher real rates; a softer dollar and depressed level give slight rebound odds at 3m.
Global AI-driven tech export boom (Asia) and strong earnings support US equities; VIX spike to 18.8 likely to partially fade absent escalation.

WTI jumped 15% in a week to $83 after the Hormuz/MOU-driven decline, signaling a renewed Middle East supply-risk premium. Spec length is low (18th percentile) and still falling, so the spike looks headline-driven and prone to partial mean reversion. I lean modestly lower for oil at every horizon.
Range of $55-115 over the past year shows two-sided tail risk. A collapse of the Iran deal could re-spike crude, which keeps the lean only slight.

Breakevens have not yet priced the oil jump (flat on the week at an 11th-percentile level). That leaves near-term catch-up risk, and a July CPI energy rebound would add to it after June's -1.41 CPI drop.
Gold is at a 1-year low and down 17% over 3 months despite geopolitical stress. Real-rate and hawkish-Fed headwinds dominate, and its failure to rally with oil argues against a quick rebound.
A higher oil price feeds the Fed's upside inflation risk and hawkish bias, which pressures the front end. That is offset by the yields' high range percentiles, leaving yields near neutral.
The VIX popped 3.7 points alongside the oil shock. It should fade if crude stabilizes, and equities retain a positive AI-earnings drift.
WTI jumped 15% in a week to $83 while VIX rose ~3.7 and S&P fell 1.6%, which looks like a renewed Middle East/Hormuz scare after the US-Iran MoU and reopening deal.
Geopolitical oil spikes tend to partially fade as long as the agreement framework holds; spec CL length is low (18th pct) but positioning was cut, so I lean modestly lower for oil, more so at 3m.
Volatility shocks from geopolitical headlines usually mean-revert, so I lean VIX lower and equities higher, supported by AI earnings momentum.

Rates show little geopolitical pass-through: 10y yields and breakevens were flat despite the oil surge. The Fed's hawkish-hold reaction function caps how far front-end yields can fall, so rates sit near neutral.
Gold failed to rally on the flare-up and is at the bottom of its 1y range, so it is not acting as a geopolitical hedge; I put it near neutral.
Tail risk: a breakdown of the Iran deal and a re-closure of Hormuz would lift oil, breakevens, VIX and HY spreads, which keeps those probabilities from straying far from 0.5.

thesis: The Fed is on a hawkish hold at 3.50-3.75% with its easing bias dropped. The 2y at 4.18% sits at the 97th percentile of its 1-year range and already prices hikes. June CPI fell on energy, labor is stable rather than hot, and TU shorts are being covered. Together these give a mild downside tilt to the front end. Term-premium and supply concerns keep the 10y stickier, so I favor modest steepening from the 7th-percentile 2s10s, most at 3 months. Equities keep a positive drift on AI earnings and loose financial conditions (NFCI -0.54). Last week's +3.7 point VIX spike should partly mean-revert absent escalation, so I lean VIX lower and S&P higher. WTI's 15% headline spike on Middle East risk, with light spec length, leans toward partial retracement, though Iran-deal tail risk keeps that lean small. Breakevens at the 11th percentile carry slight catch-up risk to oil. HY spreads at 2.73 look complacent, giving a mild widening bias at 3 months. The dollar has crowded longs and narrowing rate differentials, so I see a slight giveback over 3 months. Gold is oversold at a 1-year low, but real-rate headwinds leave it near neutral. I broadly follow the equal-weighted consensus, shading slightly toward 0.5 given no track record.
